page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Storage resources include a bundled 161 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage volumes. The server contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core testing placing in the top quartile and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 26.03 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the physical constraints of a 2-core deployment; stress-ng multi-core output and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rank in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth evaluations register 37.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.82 GB/sec for writes. Application-level performance includes 4.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.05 GB/sec in static web throughput, while small-model LLM text generation reaches 114.87 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the E4ads_v5 offers an advantageous configuration for applications that demand substantial memory capacity per thread without the expense of larger core counts. The inclusion of bundled local SSD storage reduces reliance on external disks for transient data processing. Tradeoffs include modest uncached memory bandwidth and limited parallel scaling under heavy multi-threaded compute demands. The instance is best suited for in-memory caches, intermediate database operations, staging environments, and backend web services handling memory-heavy transactional loads.
